LESSON: ULUL-AZM PROPHETS

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Pillars of Iman
Topic 3.2: Ulul-Azm Prophets

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Ulul-Azm Prophets. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What lessons do Muslims learn from the Ulul-Azm Prophets?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe the qualities of Ulul-Azm Prophets for emulation
2. apply the teachings from the stories of Nabii Musa (A.S.) and Issa (A.S.) for character building
3. appreciate the Ulul-Azm Prophets as role models

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: ULUL-AZM PROPHETS
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Ulul-Azm Prophets helps you succeed in ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: ULUL-AZM PROPHETS
Study Ulul-Azm Prophets like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Describe the qualities of Ulul-Azm Prophets for emulation

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the qualities of Ulul-Azm Prophets for emulation. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the qualities of Ulul-Azm Prophets for emulation.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Ulul-Azm Prophets” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the qualities of Ulul-Azm Prophets for emulation. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Apply the teachings from the stories of Nabii Musa (A.S.) and Issa (A.S.) for character building

What this means
In this part you learn to apply the teachings from the stories of Nabii Musa (A.S.) and Issa (A.S.) for character building. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply the teachings from the stories of Nabii Musa (A.S.) and Issa (A.S.) for character building.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Ulul-Azm Prophets in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply the teachings from the stories of Nabii Musa (A.S.) and Issa (A.S.) for character building. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the Ulul-Azm Prophets as role models

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the Ulul-Azm Prophets as role models. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the Ulul-Azm Prophets as role models.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the Ulul-Azm Prophets as role models. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Ulul-Azm Prophets is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Ulul-Azm Prophets” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: describe the qualities of Ulul-Azm Prophets for emulation)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Ulul-Azm Prophets in your own words. (skill: apply the teachings from the stories of Nabii Musa (A.S.) and Issa (A.S.) for character building)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: appreciate the Ulul-Azm Prophets as role models)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Ulul-Azm Prophets to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe the qualities of Ulul-Azm Prophets for emulation.
3. Practise this skill: apply the teachings from the stories of Nabii Musa (A.S.) and Issa (A.S.) for character building.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the Ulul-Azm Prophets as role models.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Ulul-Azm Prophets from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Ulul-Azm Prophets: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Ulul-Azm Prophets?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What lessons do Muslims learn from the Ulul-Azm Prophets?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Ulul-Azm Prophets means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe the qualities of Ulul-Azm Prophets for emulation.
5. Be able to: apply the teachings from the stories of Nabii Musa (A.S.) and Issa (A.S.) for character building.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
